overview: Black replies to 1.Nc3 with 1...e5 2.Nf3 Bc5, eyeing f2. If White grabs 3.Nxe5, Black plays ...Bxf2+ and ...Qh4+ for a dangerous attack. I am unsure of the exact theory; White can also play 3.e3 or 3.e4 and reach a normal position.

white_ideas.idea: Play e3 and d4, trading off the bishop
Avoid the e5 pawn and develop with Nxe5 only if safe

black_ideas.idea: Pressure f2 with ...Bc5 and ...Nf6, castling early
Sacrifice on f2 if White takes e5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Bc5 against f2

character.notes: The ...Bxf2+ tricks give sharp play if White grabs.

gambit.notes: Black may give a bishop for pawns after 3.Nxe5.

soundness.notes: White can decline and get a fine game.

sublines_that_differ.name: White declines
sublines_that_differ.how: No material is given and the game is quiet.

character.reason: Black threatens ...Bxf2+ and queen checks if White takes e5.

gambit.reason: Black offers e5 for activity on f2.

soundness.reason: White can decline and keep an edge.

structure.reason: The centre opens quickly and bishops aim at f2.

plans.reason: Black develops fast and aims at the weak f2 square.
